dossier.public_summary: A 4498 ppm flat-bottomed dip repeats every 6.45 days on a nearby M dwarf, implying a ~3 Earth-radius planet. Depth is steady over two sectors and four transits, with no odd/even difference or significant secondary, and no star close enough to blend could produce it. The signal is faint and its duration is relatively long, so additional transit monitoring and an on-target confirmation are needed.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative V sigma) and sub-Neptune-sized on a 0.42 Rsun M-dwarf positively favour a planet; only 4 transits at SNR 11.32 are moderate but shape is not V-shaped and size is well below stellar.

Centroid is inconclusive but a zero-pixel neighbour blend is ruled out: neighbours.plausible_within_1px=0 and could_cause_within_1px=0; the closest star that could cause the dip is 49.1 arcsec away requiring a 0.2807 eclipse, inconsistent with planet size.
reasons.value: verdict=inconclusive, why=no sector with a clear difference image

reasons.why: No odd/even difference and secondary below SNR 5 threshold; secondary phase 0.4226 is offset from 0.5, not a stellar EB.

Depth is steady between sectors 51 and 91 and between the 4 individual transits, and the longer-than-central duration (ratio 1.57) is for a low-density M dwarf and high impact parameter (b=0.7658); duration alone does not rule out planet.

No Gaia binary indicator and no evidence for blend; high density penalty reflects long duration for central density but is consistent with eccentric/high-b transit on this star and is outweighed by flat bottom and on-target limit.
